decisive_items: tender 2 × 3 cm swelling over the left clavicle with a small clean overlying wound and erythema
elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 50 mm/h
midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture
response.rationale: Osteomyelitis is favored by the overlying skin wound and erythema, elevated ESR, and lytic clavicular lesion with pathologic fracture; chronic duration with normal CBC does not exclude chronic infection. Langerhans cell histiocytosis is the closest non-infectious alternative but less likely because the local wound/erythema strongly point to infection.

rejected.why: Ewing sarcoma would more likely be acute/aggressive; the 6-month indolent course and clean overlying wound/erythema are atypical.
CRMO requires multifocal/recurrent lesions; only a single midclavicular lesion is described.
